_comment: Upload-limit research for AnimeEffects export presets. One JSON object per (platform, category). Keys mirror the row schema of assets/export/ExportTargets.txt so rows can be lifted into that table. 'checked' = date the primary source was read by the researcher. 'confidence' = verified | unverified. 'verified' means a primary source was actually read on that date, NOT that the platform is stable. Fields whose value could not be established from a primary source are null and listed in _could_not_verify at the end.

label: WhatsApp
containerCodec: 3GP, AVI, FLV, MKV, MOV, MP4 (accepted containers); server transcode to H.264
maxSizeNote: The two tiers are 64MB (slow connection) or 100MB (faster connection); MEDIA_VIDEO_MAX_SIZE_MB. NOT a hard rejection: WhatsApp downscales to 480p/720p instead. A 2GB hard ceiling applies only via the Document route (uncompressed, no inline playback).
dimensions: No exact size. Resolution is capped by the transcode target: 720p on a faster connection, 480p on a slower one.
note: faq verbatim: 'For users with a faster internet connection, the default video size limit is 100MB and 720p resolution. For users with a slower internet connection, the default video size limit is 64MB and 480p resolution.' and 'The following video formats are supported: 3GP, AVI, FLV, MKV, MOV, MP4.' and 'For documents, the maximum file size allowed is 2 GB.' Sent as Document = no transcode, 2GB ceiling, but no inline playback.
maxSizeText: 64 MB (slow connection) / 100 MB (faster connection) — downscaled, not rejected; 2 GB only via Document
maxDurationText: none for chat video (Status video 90 s)

label: WhatsApp
containerCodec: JPEG, PNG (accepted); server re-encode to JPEG
maxSizeNote: No documented hard byte limit for photos; they are compressed, typically far below 1MB. Hard ceiling 2GB only when sent as a Document.
dimensions: No exact requirement. faq recommends at least 192px height/width for profile pictures. Photos are downscaled server-side.
note: faq verbatim: 'The quality of media uploaded to WhatsApp may be lower than the original version because media files are usually compressed when shared.' Standard vs HD quality is a user-facing choice; 'HD media isn't currently available for status updates or profile pictures.'
maxSizeText: none published (media is compressed); 2 GB only via Document

label: WhatsApp sticker
containerCodec: animated: WebP ONLY (animated stickers are WebP only). Static: PNG or WebP.
maxSizeNote: Animated sticker <= 500KB per sticker (hard, enforced by the sticker-pack validation library). Static sticker <= 100KB. Pack tray icon 96x96, <= 50KB.
dimensions: EXACTLY 512x512 px per sticker. Recommend a 16px margin between art and canvas edge and an 8px #FFFFFF stroke.
note: README verbatim: 'Stickers must be exactly 512 x 512 pixels', 'Each static sticker must be less than or equal to 100KB and each animated sticker must be less than or equal to 500KB', 'Animated stickers must have frames with minimum duration of 8ms. Animation duration should be less than or equal to 10 seconds total.' Alpha REQUIRED ('Each sticker has a transparent background', faq.whatsapp.com/4148445205479237). Pack must be all-static or all-animated, never mixed; 3-30 stickers. WhatsApp advances to the first frame after one loop, so the first frame must stand alone as a static image. NOTE: the customer-facing FAQ (faq.whatsapp.com/4148445205479237) documents only the STATIC 100KB rule; the 500KB animated figure comes from the official sticker-pack repo, which is the authoritative spec for animated stickers.

label: Telegram
containerCodec: MP4 (H.264); Telegram clients support MPEG4 videos, other formats may be sent as Document. GIFs are converted server-side to MPEG4/H.264 without sound.
maxSizeNote: 2 GB per file (free accounts); 4 GB with Telegram Premium. Applies per file, not per chat. HARD rejection above the ceiling. Separately, the Bot API is far more restrictive: 50MB for non-photo uploads via multipart/form-data, 20MB by HTTP URL, and 2000MB only on a self-hosted local Bot API server.
dimensions: No documented limit for regular video. Telegram optimises each upload into several quality renditions; the client picks by bandwidth.
note: telegram.org/faq verbatim: 'share an unlimited number of photos, videos and files (doc, zip, mp3, etc.) of up to 2 GB each' and 'Send and receive files of any type, up to 2 GB in size each (or 4 GB with Premium)'. telegram.org/faq_premium confirms '4 GB File Uploads'. Re-encode nuance: sending as media triggers client-side/optimising compression, but sending as File/Document preserves the original bit-for-bit within the size ceiling. telegram.org/blog/dynamic-video-quality-and-more (2024-10-31): 'Telegram will now optimize each uploaded video for them and compress it in several qualities.' Bot numbers from core.telegram.org/bots/api (Bot API 10.1, dated 2026-06-11).

label: Telegram
containerCodec: JPEG (photo path, auto-converted); PNG/WebP/GIF and any other format only if sent as Document
maxSizeNote: No documented hard byte limit on the app photo path; images are recompressed instead (historically ~2560px longest side, ~85% JPEG, but this figure is UNVERIFIED for 2026). Hard ceiling 2GB/4GB via the File/Document route. Bot API: 10MB max for photos via multipart/form-data, 5MB by HTTP URL.
dimensions: Photo geometry is checked separately from bytes; Bot API sendPhoto rejects width+height > 10000px and width:height ratio > 20 (error PHOTO_INVALID_DIMENSIONS). Send as document to bypass.
note: The 2GB/4GB file ceiling is verified from telegram.org/faq; the 10MB-photo / 5MB-URL / 10000px / 20:1-ratio Bot API limits are verified from core.telegram.org/bots/api. The exact in-app photo recompression target (2560px / 85% JPEG) is commonly cited but I could NOT verify it from a Telegram primary source, so treat it as unverified. PNG sent as a photo is converted to JPEG, destroying alpha; send as Document to keep PNG+alpha.
maxSizeText: none on the app photo path (recompressed); Bot API 10 MB multipart / 5 MB by URL; 2 GB (4 GB Premium) as a Document

label: Telegram sticker (video)
containerCodec: WebM, VP9 codec. No audio stream.
maxSizeNote: <= 256 KB (hard). Custom emoji use the same tech but must be exactly 100x100.
dimensions: For stickers, one side must be EXACTLY 512 px; the other side may be 512 px or less. For emoji, exactly 100x100.
note: core.telegram.org/stickers verbatim: 'For stickers, one side must be exactly 512 pixels in size - the other side can be 512 pixels or less', 'Video duration must not exceed 3 seconds', 'Frame rate can be up to 30 FPS', 'Video size should not exceed 256 KB', 'Video must be in .WEBM format encoded with the VP9 codec', 'Video must have no audio stream'. Requires Telegram 8.5 or higher. 'Video should be looped for optimal user experience.'

label: Telegram sticker (animated / TGS)
containerCodec: TGS (gzipped Lottie JSON, exported via the Bodymovin-TG After Effects plugin)
maxSizeNote: <= 64 KB after rendering in Bodymovin (hard).
dimensions: Canvas EXACTLY 512x512. Objects must not leave the canvas.
note: verbatim: 'The canvas size must be 512x512 pixels', 'Animation length must not exceed 3 seconds', 'All animations must be looped', 'Final file size must not exceed 64 KB after rendering in Bodymovin', 'All animations must run at 60 Frames Per Second'. A long list of After Effects features is forbidden (Auto-bezier keys, Expressions, Masks, Layer Effects, Images, Solids, Texts, 3D Layers, Merge Paths, Star Shapes, Gradient Strokes, Repeaters, Time Stretching/Remapping, Auto-Oriented Layers) - relevant if we ever emit TGS.

label: Telegram sticker (static)
containerCodec: PNG or WebP
maxSizeNote: No separately documented byte cap for static stickers beyond the general file ceiling; the practical constraint is the 512px geometry. Documented requirements are format and geometry only.
dimensions: One side EXACTLY 512 px, other side <= 512 px. Emoji: exactly 100x100.
note: verbatim: 'The image file must be in either .PNG or .WEBP format.' Alpha is expected: 'a transparent background, white stroke and black shadow effect will make your sticker stand out.'
maxSizeText: not separately documented beyond the geometry rules

label: Telegram sticker (import from other apps)
containerCodec: PNG, WebP or WebM accepted by the @Stickers bot
dimensions: Presumably the same geometry rules as native creation; not restated on the import path.
note: verbatim: 'Users can ... easily publish custom stickers with the @Stickers bot using .PNG, .WEBP or .WEBM files for stickers from other apps.' This is the route an external tool would use to push a generated sticker into Telegram; the accepted set is exactly our three sticker outputs. Byte/duration caps are NOT restated here - assume the per-format caps above apply, but that is an inference, not a documented statement.
maxSizeText: not separately documented beyond the geometry rules

label: Discord
containerCodec: No fixed codec list. Documented common types include JPEG, PNG, PDF, MP3, MOV, MP4 (H.264, HEVC/H265, or AV1), GIF, animated WebP, AVIF. Embed images restricted to .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp/.gif.
maxSizeNote: Discord publishes the free number as 20MB as of the 2026-08-13 article revision: 'For non-Nitro subscribers, the maximum file upload is 20MB.' Nitro Basic 50MB, Nitro 500MB. Boosted servers grant 50MB (L2) / 100MB (L3) to all members. HARD rejection above the applicable tier. Discord also warns it is 'currently experimenting with various file upload size limits' so select accounts may see larger values.
dimensions: No documented limit; media is inspected, converted and resized server-side.
note: RESOLVED CONFLICT: earlier in this session the same article ID (25444343291031) rendered as 'File Attachments FAQ' and said 10MB. As of the 2026-08-13 revision the article is titled 'File Attachments Upload Limits FAQ' and says 20MB, and its image setting text now reads 'Any image that is larger than 20MB will be shared as a download instead' (was 10MB). So the 20MB change announced by Discord on 2026-08-13 IS now reflected in the primary help article; I am treating 20MB as verified. STILL STALE ELSEWHERE: support.discord.com 'Discord Account Caps' (33694251638295) retains a File Sharing Limit row of Base 10MB / Basic 50MB / Nitro 500MB, and docs.discord.com/developers/reference still states 'The default limit is 10 MiB for all users' - treat those as lagging. Mobile caveat from the same announcement: size is now measured BEFORE compression, so mobile uploads of large camera-roll files may fail more often than under the old post-compression check. Re-encoding is separately documented on Discord's engineering blog (modern-image-formats-at-discord-supporting-webp-and-avif): 'Discord must inspect, convert, and resize every still and animated image attached'; AVIF is converted to WebP and HDR AVIF tone-mapped to SDR.

label: Discord sticker
containerCodec: PNG (static), APNG (animated), GIF (animated), Lottie JSON. API format_type enum: PNG=1, APNG=2, LOTTIE=3, GIF=4.
maxSizeNote: 512 KB max (hard). Requires a boosted server; sticker slots are 5 (base), 15 (L1), 30 (L2), 60 (L3).
dimensions: EXACTLY 320x320 px. Renders at 160x160 dp in the desktop chat, which is why 320x320 is required.
note: Two sources agree on the constraints. Support article verbatim: 'Animated File types: APNG', 'Static File type: PNG', 'Max File size: 512KB', 'Dimensions: 320px x 320px (exact)'. discord.com/blog/how-to-create-upload-your-own-stickers-on-discord (2025-03-31) adds GIF as an accepted animated format: 'PNG for static stickers, APNG or GIF for animated stickers', and the 5/15/30/60 slot ladder. The 5-SECOND animated cap is from discord.js (RESTPostAPIGuildStickerFormDataBody): 'max 512 KB ... Uploaded stickers are constrained to 5 seconds in length for animated stickers, and 320 x 320 pixels' - a client library, so slightly weaker provenance than the API docs, but it mirrors the API validation. Also note the support article's warning: an uploaded APNG will NOT render if you upload it through the chat bar, so upload must go through Server Settings > Stickers.

label: Discord custom emoji
containerCodec: Upload accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF. All emoji are SERVED as WebP (client uses WebP for all in-app emoji); animated ones as animated WebP.
maxSizeNote: 256 KiB max (hard, API returns 400 Bad Request). Discord's own blog notes that oversized images are now compressed rather than rejected, so the practical behaviour is soften-and-accept via the client even though the API hard-rejects.
dimensions: 128x128 recommended; the API field is documented as 'the 128x128 emoji image'. Discord's blog: 'Bigger or smaller will work, but 128x128 is juuuust right' - i.e. the client now resizes for you, so 128x128 is the canonical target rather than a hard requirement.
note: API docs verbatim: 'Emojis and animated emojis have a maximum file size of 256 KiB. Attempting to upload an emoji larger than this limit will fail and return 400 Bad Request.' Supported upload formats listed as JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF. discord.com/blog/beginners-guide-to-custom-emojis (2025-12-12) contradicts the hard-reject framing: 'File size: 256 KB. If your emoji's a bit bigger, we'll go ahead and compress it.' and 'you can upload any ol' image and Discord'll do all the resizing for ya'. IMPORTANT for animated emoji: a Discord engineer on github.com/discord/lilliput/issues/159 stated 'We currently still require emoji uploads be provided as GIF for backward compatibility, as WebP -> GIF is not currently a supported transformation.' So emit animated emoji as GIF, not animated WebP, despite WebP being an accepted upload format. Alpha is preserved (WebP/AVIF carry variable alpha, which the engineering blog calls out as essential for animated emoji).

label: Signal
containerCodec: MP4/H.264 on the wire after client-side transcode. Original container is preserved only when sent as a File and the transcode is skipped.
maxSizeNote: 100 MiB per attachment by default. This is NOT a hard-coded constant - it is the default of the server-controlled feature flag global.attachments.maxBytes, so Signal can and does change it remotely. Some 2026 reporting claims a raise to 200MB; I could not confirm that in source or official docs, so treat 100 MiB as the verified value and 200MB as unverified.
dimensions: No documented limit. Videos are re-encoded to 720p at ~2 Mbps by default; the encoded output targets ~50MB (~30MB on low-memory devices), reducing bitrate down to a 480p/500kbps floor for long clips.
note: Signal publishes NO user-facing attachment size documentation, so the authoritative source is client source. RemoteConfig.kt: maxAttachmentSizeBytes -> key 'global.attachments.maxBytes', defaultValue = 100.mebiBytes.inWholeBytes, hotSwappable = true; videoTranscodeTargetSizeBytes -> 'global.videoAttachments.transcodeTargetBytes' default 100 MiB; maxSourceTranscodeVideoSizeBytes -> default 1 GiB. The older 50MB/30MB 720p transcode policy is quoted by an Signal developer in signalapp/Signal-Android issue #13258 and is documented as aged behaviour. The 200MB claim comes from aboutsignal.com (2026-07-31), a secondary source - UNVERIFIED, and inconsistent with current main's 100 MiB default. Because the value is a remote flag, an app preset should treat 100 MiB as the safe floor.

label: Signal
containerCodec: JPEG output after client recompression; original PNG preserved only if sent as a File.
maxSizeNote: Same 100 MiB flag ceiling, but images are far more tightly constrained in practice by the client's own targeting: maxImageFileSize is 1MB / 1.5MB / 3MB depending on quality level, and images are scaled to a ladder of target dimensions.
dimensions: Image dimension ladder by quality level: LEVEL_1 1600/1024/768/512; LEVEL_2 2048/1600/1024/768/512; LEVEL_3 and H.265 4096/3072/2048/1600/1024/768/512. Low-memory devices: 768/512 at 1MB.
note: PushMediaConstraints.java MediaConfig enum: LEVEL_1_LOW_MEMORY(maxImageFileSize 1MB, targets 768/512, quality 70), LEVEL_1(1MB, 1600/1024/768/512, 70), LEVEL_2(1.5MB, 2048/1600/1024/768/512, 75), LEVEL_3(3MB, 4096/3072/2048/1600/1024/768/512, 75), LEVEL_3_H265(3MB, same targets, 75). getGifMaxSize() = min(25MB, maxAttachmentSize). 'HIGH' sent-media quality selects the H.265 preset when the device can encode HEVC.

label: Signal sticker
containerCodec: Animated: APNG only ('Please do not upload GIFs'). Static: PNG or WebP. Cover: 512x512 PNG or WebP.
maxSizeNote: 300 KB per sticker (hard). Cover must be 512x512. Maximum 200 stickers per pack.
dimensions: Stickers resize to 512x512 px. Recommend a 16px margin around each sticker and outlining so it works on light and dark backgrounds.
note: support.signal.org verbatim: 'Non-animated stickers must be a separate PNG or WebP file', 'Animated stickers must be a separate APNG file. Please do not upload GIFs', 'Each sticker has a size limit of 300kb', 'Animated stickers maximum animation length of 3 seconds', 'Stickers resize to 512 x 512 px', 'Maximum 200 stickers per pack'. Also: 'Animated stickers should have 30 or 60 FPS', 'Animated stickers should loop seamlessly', and the first frame serves as the still preview on devices without APNG playback - so the first frame must stand alone. CAVEAT: the page carries no date. The 100KB->300KB change is evidenced by signalapp/signal-desktop PR/issue #4625 ('Animated stickers are allowed to be up to 300kB since <commit>'), so 300KB is current.

label: Pixiv ugoira (うごイラ)
containerCodec: Two routes. (1) Multiple still frames: PNG or JPEG, all frames must share one format and one canvas size. (2) Pre-made animated GIF. NOT APNG/WebP. pixiv converts the upload into its own animation for playback.
maxSizeNote: Route 1 (frame sequence): 30 MB total per post, and 8 MB max per individual frame, max 150 frames. Route 2 (animated GIF): 16 MB total, max 500 frames. HARD rejection above these ('you will not be able to upload it').
dimensions: No fixed pixel size, but all frames must be identical in size. pixiv warns that a very large image or an 'extreme' width/height ratio can cause an upload to fail even when byte and frame limits are respected. Desktop web only - the mobile site and app cannot post ugoira.
note: ugoira (うごイラ) has NO fps setting and NO zip-of-frames upload: you either multi-select up to 150 separate PNG **or** JPEG images (all frames must share the same format AND the same canvas size) and author each frame's display time in the posting UI, or you upload one animated GIF (16 MB, max 500 frames). Limits: frame route 150 images / 8 MB per image / 30 MB total; GIF route 16 MB and 500 frames. Over-limit uploads fail outright, and even under-limit files can fail if the image is 'extremely large' or the aspect ratio is extreme — no pixel cap is published, only 'reduce the size' advice. Desktop web only (the mobile site and app cannot post ugoira). CRITICAL for an exporter: pixiv re-encodes server-side into its own ugoira package — verified LIVE today, ugoira_meta for work 44298467 returns a server-built ZIP at i.pximg.net/img-zip-ugoira/... containing frames plus a {file, delay} table, served as _ugoira600x600.zip up to _ugoira1920x1080.zip with mime_type image/jpeg; a work posted 2026-09-11 returned 26 frames as .jpg at 110/120 ms delays. Because frames end up as JPEG, PNG TRANSPARENCY DOES NOT SURVIVE the ugoira conversion. Separately, normal (non-ugoira) illustration upload accepts JPG/GIF/PNG at 32 MB per file and explicitly REJECTS BMP, animated GIF and APNG; mixing formats in one post converts everything to JPG (pixiv.help articles 235584588 and 235584428, both PRE-2025). Loop wording is not published even though it plays as an animation.
maxSizeText: 30 MB total and 8 MB per frame (frame route); 16 MB (animated-GIF route)

label: Bluesky
containerCodec: The embed lexicon accepts ONLY video/mp4. Bluesky's own product blog states the app 'currently supports .mp4, .mpeg, .webm, and .mov' - the app layer is broader than the protocol layer, and the protocol (lexicon) is the harder constraint.
maxSizeNote: 100 MB. Elevated from 50 MB in March 2025 by the app.bsky.embed.video lexicon (maxSize 50000000 -> 100000000). Boundary is the lexicon value, enforced at PDS write time. Also a separate account-level quota: 25 videos / 10 GB of video per day, and the account email must be verified.
dimensions: No pixel-size limit. Aspect ratio must be supplied explicitly as metadata with the embed (aspectRatio {width,height}), so the exporter must know the true dimensions.
note: Bluesky's video numbers moved TWICE recently, so most published figures are stale: 50 MB -> 100 MB on 2025-03-03, then 100 MB -> 300 MB and 3 min -> 10 min in August 2026. Current values from Bluesky's own client constants (VIDEO_MAX_DURATION_MS = 10*60*1000, VIDEO_MAX_SIZE_MB = 300) and the atproto video lexicon, which accepts ONLY video/mp4 as the stored blob; the official client also accepts video/mpeg, video/webm, video/quicktime and image/gif for UPLOAD and transcodes them, so the protocol constraint (mp4) is the one to satisfy. Exceeding the size fails with a server message like 'file size (N bytes) is larger than the maximum allowed size (300000000 bytes)' — a hard rejection. Re-encoding is official: the client uploads to video.bsky.app, polls getJobStatus, and 'the video service runs the processing step on your video, then saves an optimised version'. Aspect ratio must be passed as explicit metadata. No documented pixel-dimension cap. Images (up to 4 per post): 2 MB per image (2,000,000 bytes, hard lexicon maxSize) and max dimension 4000 px (raised from 2000 px in April 2026); the CDN 'usually' resizes and may convert images to JPEG, so alpha survival is unverified. Bluesky has NO sticker or custom-emoji upload format — only emoji reactions (limit 5) — so there is no Bluesky sticker row.
maxSizeText: 300 MB (300,000,000 bytes) — raised from 100 MB in Aug 2026; hard server-side rejection
maxDurationText: 10 min (600 s) — raised from 3 min in Aug 2026

label: Mastodon
containerCodec: Video: MP4, M4V, MOV, WebM (protocol-level supported_mime_types also lists video/quicktime, video/ogg, video/x-ms-asf). Animated GIF (GIFV) is ALSO accepted and is converted server-side to a soundless MP4. Still images: PNG, JPG, HEIF/HEIC, WebP, AVIF.
maxSizeNote: INSTANCE-CONFIGURABLE - there is no single platform-wide number. Upstream default: VIDEO_LIMIT = 99.megabytes (99 MiB = 103,809,024 bytes, confirmed live via the instance API video_size_limit). Images: IMAGE_LIMIT = 16.megabytes (16 MiB = 16,777,216 bytes). Admins override both via MAX_VIDEO_SIZE / MAX_IMAGE_SIZE, so the only reliable check is the target instance's own /api/v2/instance response.
dimensions: Video matrix limit 8,294,400 px (~8.3 MP, i.e. 3840x2160); frame rate limit 120 fps. Images are downscaled to 8.3 megapixels (image_matrix_limit 33,177,600). Animated GIF dimensions must be under 1 MP (1280x720).
note: PER-INSTANCE — say so in any UI. Upstream defaults and the live instance do NOT agree, which is exactly why this must be read at runtime. Upstream default (docs.joinmastodon.org/user/posting/, page dated 2026-07-08, and mastodon/mastodon app/models/media_attachment.rb): VIDEO_LIMIT = 99.megabytes, IMAGE_LIMIT = 16.megabytes, GIFV 16 MB, images downscaled to 8.3 megapixels, GIF under 1 MP (1280x720), video transcoded to H.264 MP4 at max 1300 kbps, 120 fps, one video or one GIF per post. LIVE CHECK of mastodon.social/api/v2/instance (version 4.8.0-alpha.2, fetched 2026-09-11): image_size_limit 16,777,216 and video_size_limit 103,809,024 (both matching upstream) BUT image_matrix_limit = 33,177,600 px (~33.2 MP — DOUBLE the upstream 8.3 MP default). So the byte caps matched upstream while a pixel cap did not, proving per-instance drift is real. Admins override via MAX_IMAGE_SIZE / MAX_VIDEO_SIZE; the definitive answer for a given instance is GET /api/v2/instance -> configuration.media_attachments (docs.joinmastodon.org/entities/Instance/). Looping: soundless MP4 and WebM 'will be looped in clients the same way as an animated GIF', so a silent looping MP4 is the correct export.

label: Mastodon custom emoji
containerCodec: Images whose MIME type is in the instance's IMAGE_MIME_TYPES - in practice PNG for static and GIF for animated custom emoji.
maxSizeNote: 256 KiB (256.kilobytes) per custom emoji, enforced by a validation that rejects anything larger. NOTE: the widely repeated 50 KB figure is WRONG for current Mastodon - I checked the source.
dimensions: No documented source dimension; the server generates resized variants and emoji render at roughly 16x16 to 50x50 px, so supply a square source.
note: Source verbatim: class CustomEmoji < ApplicationRecord ... LIMIT = 256.kilobytes ... validates_attachment :image, content_type: { content_type: IMAGE_MIME_TYPES }, presence: true, size: { less_than: LIMIT }. Hard validation, so larger files are rejected outright. Alpha expected (emoji must render on light and dark themes).

label: X (Twitter) — video on a Post
containerCodec: MP4 or MOV. Video codec H.264 High Profile. Audio AAC-LC (High-Efficiency AAC NOT supported), mono or stereo only (no 5.1), 128 kbps minimum. No open GOP; progressive scan only; pixel format YUV 4:2:0 only; pixel aspect ratio 1:1.
maxSizeNote: 8 GB for the default (non-Premium) Post video category; 16 GB for X Premium/verified. HARD limits, and enforced TWICE - a media_id can finalize successfully and still be rejected later by the Post-create call (403 Forbidden with a duration message).
dimensions: Dimensions must be between 32x32 and 1280x1024. Aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Frame rate 60 fps or less. Recommended: 1280x720 landscape, 720x1280 portrait, 720x720 square. Unsubscribed users get 720p playback; subscribers can upload 1080p and get 1080p playback.
note: MAJOR MISCITATION WARNING - this is the single most misreported row in the whole table. The figure '140 seconds / 512 MB' that blogs and spec-aggregator sites endlessly repeat is X's **DM** video cap (dm_video), NOT the Post video cap. X's own API best-practices page gives: image 5 MB; animated GIF (tweet_gif) 15 MB; video on a Post (tweet_video/amplify_video) 0.5 s-20 min and 8 GB; video in a DM (dm_video) 0.5-140 s and 512 MB. For X Premium/verified: Post video 0.5 s-125 min, 16 GB; DM video 0.5-10 min, 1 GB. So the correct non-Premium Post-video pair is 20 minutes / 8 GB. Caveat: help.x.com is Cloudflare-403 to automated readers, so the end-user app UI may show different (lower) numbers than the API; the API doc is the only X-published source I could read. Re-encoding is documented: 'All uploads are processed for optimization across multiple platforms.'

label: TikTok
containerCodec: MP4 (recommended), WebM, MOV. Codecs: H.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8, VP9. GIF is NOT accepted.
maxSizeNote: 4 GB maximum (documented in the Content Posting API media transfer guide). Also relevant for API/automated uploads: chunks must be 5-64 MB each (final chunk may be up to 128 MB), videos under 5 MB must be sent whole, videos over 64 MB must be chunked, 1-1000 chunks, sequential.
dimensions: Minimum 360 px and maximum 4096 px for BOTH width and height. Frame rate 23-60 FPS. Recommended 9:16 vertical, 1080x1920.
note: Guide 'Last updated August 4, 2026' - one of the freshest primary docs in this whole table. Verbatim: 'Supported media formats: MP4 (recommended), WebM, MOV'; 'Supported codecs: H.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8, VP9'; 'Framerate restrictions: Minimum of 23 FPS, Maximum of 60 FPS'; 'Picture size restrictions: Minimum of 360 pixels for both height and width, Maximum of 4096 pixels for both height and width'; 'Size restrictions: Maximum of 4GB'. Duration verbatim: 'All TikTok creators can post 3-minute videos, while some have access to post 5-minute or 10-minute videos. The longest video a developer can send via the initialize Upload Video endpoint is 10 minutes.' So the 3/5/10-minute tiers are account-dependent and 10 min (600 s) is the developer ceiling. NOT VERIFIED: the widely quoted mobile app caps of ~287.6 MB (iOS) / ~72 MB (Android) and the 30/60-minute upload claims appear only in third-party sources - support.tiktok.com is fully client-rendered and I could not read an official page stating them.

label: TikTok photo post
containerCodec: WebP or JPEG. GIF not accepted.
maxSizeNote: 20 MB per image (hard). Up to 35 images per photo post.
dimensions: Maximum 1080p.
note: Useful for an animation tool only if exporting stills; TikTok does NOT accept GIF or APNG as a photo post, so an animated short must go through the video path.

label: YouTube
containerCodec: Widely accepting: MOV, MPEG-1/2/4, MP4, MPG, AVI, WMV, MPEGPS, FLV, 3GPP, WebM, DNxHR, ProRes, CineForm, HEVC. Recommended delivery: MP4 container with H.264 video and AAC-LC audio, 48 kHz, 4:2:0, closed GOP, progressive scan.
maxSizeNote: 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less (hard). Note this is an account-level ceiling, not a per-quality ceiling.
dimensions: Recommended up to 4320p (7680x4320). Standard 16:9; the player adapts. Shorts uploads are capped at 1080p.
note: Verbatim: 'The maximum file size you can upload is 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less. We've changed the limits on uploads in the past, so you may see older videos that are longer than 12 hours.' and 'By default, you can upload videos that are up to 15 minutes long. Verified accounts can upload videos longer than 15 minutes.' So the familiar 15-minute figure applies only to UNVERIFIED accounts. Re-encoding is explicit in YouTube's docs ('YouTube always re-encodes videos to optimize their playback quality') and new uploads are processed in low quality first. Alpha is not in the accepted format list, so transparency is effectively unsupported. Shorts: same account ceiling, up to 3 min, vertical 9:16, upload max 1080p (support.google.com/youtube/answer/10059070).

label: VK (VK Video post)
containerCodec: AVI, MP4, 3GP, MPEG, MOV, FLV, F4V, WMV, MKV, WEBM, VOB, RM, RMVB, M4V, MPG, OGV, TS, M2TS, MTS. MP4/H.264 is the practical target. GIF is not accepted as a video.
maxSizeNote: 256 GB (hard cap) for an organic VK Video post.
dimensions: Up to 4K. VK recommends 16:9 at 1280x720 or above.
note: MISCITATION WARNING: the '2 GB / 1080p' figure widely attributed to VK is VK's ADVERTISING format requirement (vk.com/faq14074), NOT the organic upload limit. Organic video is 256 GB and up to 4K. VK serves transcoded renditions (e.g. mp4_720) but does not state 'we re-encode' explicitly, so the re-encode flag is inferred from the rendition ladder rather than quoted. Source page dated 2025-09-08. VK Clips is a separate, much tighter surface: 1 GB, 3 s-3 min, 9:16 1080x1920, <=60 FPS (vk.com/faq20115).

label: VK (photo attachment)
containerCodec: JPG, PNG, GIF (per the API).
maxSizeNote: 50 MB is documented at the API endpoint level (photo-in-message upload). VK's user-facing help publishes no MB figure, so treat 50 MB as the API limit rather than a universal user limit.
dimensions: Sum of height + width <= 14,000 px; each side <= 8,192 px; aspect ratio at least 1:20 (API rules).
note: Dimensions and the 50 MB API cap are verified from VK's API docs; the user-facing help page (vk.com/faq18545) documents the size rules but no MB ceiling. Whether an uploaded PNG's alpha channel survives VK's resize/recompress is NOT documented - do not promise transparency on VK. GIF conversion and loop behaviour are likewise undocumented at the primary level.

label: Instagram Reels
containerCodec: MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14), no edit lists, moov atom at the FRONT of the file. Video codec HEVC or H.264, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling. Audio AAC, 48 kHz max, 1-2 channels. VBR, 25 Mbps max video bitrate, 128 kbps audio.
maxSizeNote: 300 MB maximum per the official Graph API Reels specification (hard). Any larger in-app figures circulating online are NOT published by Meta.
dimensions: Max 1920 horizontal pixels. Required aspect ratio between 0.01:1 and 10:1, but 9:16 is recommended to avoid cropping or blank space. Frame rate 23-60 FPS. The consumer help centre gives the app-facing version: aspect ratio between 1.91:1 and 9:16, minimum 30 FPS, minimum resolution 720 px.
note: Official spec verbatim: 'Container: MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14), no edit lists, moov atom at the front of the file'; 'Video codec: HEVC or H264, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling'; 'Duration: 15 mins maximum, 3 seconds minimum'; 'File size: 300MB maximum'; 'Maximum columns (horizontal pixels): 1920'. Reference page updated 2026-08-12. The moov-at-front requirement is a real gotcha for an exporter - a normal MP4 with moov at the end can be rejected. Instagram/Meta re-encoding is documented at the engineering level (Meta describes creating multiple encoded versions/bitstreams per upload). Stories are separate and tighter: video 100 MB, 3-60 s, aspect 0.1:1-10:1. IGTV is retired; the obsolete '90-second Reels' cap is gone (in-app allows up to ~20 min, but Meta recommends <=3 min for audiences you are not connected to). Feed image via API is JPEG only, 8 MB, aspect 4:5 to 1.91:1.

label: Weibo (微博)
containerCodec: MP4 is the practical/most compatible target. Third-party guides claim MP4/MOV/AVI but Weibo's own help pages do NOT publish a container list - treat the container list as unverified.
maxSizeNote: PC (web) upload: up to 15 GB. Mobile app: up to 4 GB. These are the two documented ceilings and they differ by route, so an export preset must pick the route. Mobile also rejects anything under 3 seconds.
dimensions: No published pixel limit. Weibo requires submitted videos to be 720p or above to enter the video community (投稿), and the platform's own engineering write-up says the service's resolution range historically ran 240p to 720p, with the compression threshold for publishing raised from 480p to 720p. Horizontal uploads above 1080p are restricted by account view-count standing.
note: Verbatim from Weibo's own FAQ (kefu.weibo.com/faqdetail?id=21503, updated 2024-07-01 — PRE-2025): '视频上传有大小限制吗？ PC端可支持15G。 手机端在微博首页点击右上角“+”发布视频，最大支持4G大小；' and '（*手机端上传视频不支持低于3S以下的时长视频）'. A second official page (kefu.weibo.com/faqdetail?id=20938, updated 2024-09-27) requires 投稿 videos to be 720p or above. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the common premise that Weibo's duration limit varies by verification level is UNSUPPORTED — Weibo publishes only a MINIMUM duration (3 s, mobile). Third-party pages claim 5/15/30/60 min caps attributed to 认证/会员/视频号 tiers and contradict each other; no official page confirms any of them, so leave Weibo's maximum duration blank rather than guessing. Weibo also publishes NO container/codec list for consumer video upload — only '转码' (transcoding) is discussed; MP4 is our practical choice, not a documented requirement. Images and GIFs are separate: Weibo accepts only gif/jpg/png, at 20 MB per image, and an animated GIF must be at most 1080 px wide or it will not animate (kefu.weibo.com/faqdetail?id=12483 and id=21352); client-side compression on upload is documented, with an 原图 (original) option to bypass it. Confirmed transcoding: '为什么上传本地视频后时长变短…由于视频转码后导致'. Alpha survival is not documented.
maxDurationText: minimum 3 s (mobile); NO official maximum for any tier

label: Bilibili (哔哩哔哩)
containerCodec: Recommended: MP4 and FLV (Bilibili states these are advantaged in transcoding and clear review faster). Other accepted: AVI, WMV, MOV, WebM, MPEG4, TS, MPG, RM, RMVB, MKV, M4V. Codec H.264/AVC; audio AAC. Colour space yuv420, 8-bit SDR (10-bit HDR allowed), progressive scan.
maxSizeNote: 4 GB maximum per the official submission API. Files over 100 MB must use the chunked-upload flow; files up to 100 MB may go through the single-file flow. NOTE: several third-party guides quote 2 GB - the official API says 4 GB, so use 4 GB.
dimensions: Maximum resolution 4096x4096. Maximum frame rate 120 fps. Peak bitrate up to 60 Mbps. (Older submission-tool guidance recommended a 1920x1080 / 6000 kbps ceiling, and exceeding the recommended parameters triggers 二压 / a second compression pass - that is a quality warning, not a hard limit.)
note: CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL BILIBILI SOURCES — carry both, do not silently pick one. (1) Bilibili's submission help centre (article qid=3845&pid=312, updated 2026-04-01, read via Bilibili's help backend API api.bilibili.com/x/web-goblin/help/detail) gives a 16 GB hard cap with 64 GB available on web upload at 权益等级 lv3+ (>=1000 followers), and 4096x4096 at <=120 fps, yuv420, SDR 8-bit / HDR 10-bit, keyframe at least one per 10 s average; minimum duration 3 s and a documented 36000 s (10 h) for mobile single-part submissions, while the current web article omits duration entirely. (2) Bilibili's open-platform submission API documentation (bilibili.apifox.cn/api-23693239) states 文件大小限制为4GB and 视频时长小于5小时 (4 GB / under 5 h). I verified the 16 GB claim only second-hand: my own attempts to re-fetch the help API returned code -400 and the help page is JS-rendered, so I could not independently reproduce it today, whereas I did read the apifox 4 GB page myself. The 16 GB figure is also more consistent with Bilibili's current product. RECOMMENDATION: encode 4 GB as the conservative floor and surface 16 GB (64 GB at lv3+) as the optimistic case. IMPORTANT TIER CORRECTION: Bilibili is tiered on FILE SIZE, not on duration — do not present it as a duration-tiered platform. The widely repeated 8 GB / 32 GB / 电磁力 tier numbers are from 2020-2023 sources and are obsolete. Transcoding is mandatory (转码 is a pipeline stage; 转码失败 is a listed status), and >100 MB forces chunked upload in the API flow. Source pages: qid=3934&pid=333 (2025-06-19), qid=3841&pid=312 (2025-06-09), qid=3853&pid=312.
maxSizeText: 16 GB hard cap; 64 GB on web for 权益等级 lv3+ (a SEPARATE official Bilibili source gives 4 GB — see note)
maxDurationText: 10 h documented for mobile single-P submissions; the current web article states no max

label: Facebook Messenger
containerCodec: Not published for the consumer app. The Messenger Platform (Pages/bots) API accepts image/video/audio/file assets without a published codec list; GIF and PNG are accepted as image assets.
maxSizeNote: 25 MB for all asset types on the developer (Messenger Platform) surface, and 8 MB for an image supplied by URL. IMPORTANT: these are DEVELOPER-API numbers. The consumer Messenger app publishes NO size, duration, codec or dimension limits at all - Meta's consumer help page documents only how to send, with zero numbers. So '25 MB' should not be presented as the user-facing attachment limit.
dimensions: Not published. The only duration-like figure in the developer docs is a 75-second timeout for fetching a video supplied by URL, which is a fetch timeout, not a duration limit.
note: The 25 MB / 8 MB figures come from the Messenger Platform 'saving assets' documentation, and the limits are stated as applying 'after encoding' - which itself implies server-side encoding. The consumer help page (facebook.com/help/messenger-app/141024792690630) documents sending photos/videos/GIFs/stickers but publishes no numeric limits whatsoever; that absence is the finding for the consumer case. Messenger has NO public sticker submission/format spec, so there is no Messenger sticker row to export for.
maxSizeText: 25 MB all asset types / 8 MB image-by-URL (developer API only); consumer app publishes none

label: LINE
containerCodec: Not published by LINE for chat video. Photos in chat/album accept JPEG/PNG/GIF.
maxSizeNote: 20 MB is documented for ALBUM photos (with original quality gated behind LINE Premium). LINE publishes NO megabyte cap for sending a video or file in a normal chat. The widely repeated '5-minute chat video' and '~1 GB File send' figures appear only in third-party blogs and are NOT on any LINE help page - treat as unverified.
dimensions: ALBUM photos: up to 100 megapixels. Video resolution is not specified by LINE.
note: Verified: 20 MB album photo limit, 100 MP photo ceiling, album videos up to 5 minutes (the 5-minute figure applies to the ALBUM path, not to ordinary chat sends), and a 50-items-at-once limit. LINE auto-compresses/resizes chat photos and videos and offers a 'sent photo quality' setting; sending as File preserves the original. UNVERIFIED: the accepted container/codec list for video, the ordinary chat video size cap, and any chat video duration cap. Do not encode a LINE chat-video preset on the strength of the 5-minute number.
maxSizeText: 20 MB for ALBUM photos; no published MB cap for a chat video/file
maxDurationText: 5 min for ALBUM videos (Premium); no published cap for chat video

label: LINE sticker (animated)
containerCodec: APNG with a .png file extension - explicitly NOT GIF and NOT WebP. Main image is also APNG 240x240; chat thumbnail icon is PNG 96x74.
maxSizeNote: 1 MB maximum per image file. If submitting the whole set as one ZIP, the ZIP must be <= 60 MB. NOTE: a SECOND official LINE document aimed at Sponsored Stickers states the final APNG should be no larger than 300 KB, so LINE's own two documents disagree; I use the Creators Market guideline (1 MB) as primary because it governs normal sticker submissions.
dimensions: Maximum 320x270 px, AND either the width or the height must be at least 270 px (if height is the longer side it must be exactly 270). Between 5 and 20 PNG frames per APNG. Set size 8, 16 or 24 stickers. RGB colour space only (indexed colour not supported). Transparent background required. Do not add margins - LINE adds them.
note: Verbatim: 'Animated stickers' image files must adhere to the two following criteria. - Their dimensions must be within 320 x 270. - Either the width or height of the image must be at least 270 pixels.'; 'Playback time: Up to 4 seconds per sticker'; 'Loops: 1-4 loops per sticker whose combined length does not exceed 4 seconds'; 'PNG frame limits per APNG: Between 5 and 20 frames'; 'The maximum file size for each image is 1 MB'; 'Please ensure that your [images] are in RGB color space.' Out-of-spec files produce an upload error, so these are hard validations. Two important gotchas: (1) playback times are restricted to whole 1/2/3/4 seconds - 1.5 s is rejected; (2) identical frames may be merged into a single frame by APNG tools, so a file whose frames are all identical will fail as an animated sticker. The first frame is used as the still image wherever APNG playback is unavailable, so it must stand alone. The 300 KB discrepancy is documented at lineforbusiness.com/files/LINE_Sponsored_Stickers_Guide_ENG.pdf.

label: WeChat sticker (微信表情, sticker platform)
containerCodec: Animated stickers: GIF only. Static: PNG/JPG/GIF. Cover: PNG. Chat panel icon: PNG.
maxSizeNote: 500 KB per sticker image, 500 KB cover (240x240), 500 KB detail banner, 100 KB chat panel icon. NOT a hard rejection: WeChat's spec states over-limit or wrong-dimension assets are automatically COMPRESSED AND CROPPED ('超出文件大小、尺寸要求的图片素材将被自动压缩和裁剪').
dimensions: Sticker image exactly 240x240. Cover 240x240. Chat panel icon 50x50. Detail banner 750x400. Set must contain 8-24 stickers.
note: WeChat's official 表情开放平台 spec. Animated stickers MUST loop ('动态表情应设置循环播放'). Transparency is explicitly required for the cover and the chat panel icon; for the sticker image itself transparency is expected but not stated as mandatory. Because over-spec art is auto-compressed and CROPPED rather than rejected, an exporter that is slightly off-spec will silently lose pixels - so hit 240x240 exactly. NOTE this is the WeChat STICKER PLATFORM (a reviewed creator submission), not an everyday chat attachment. Also on the same platform: 特效 AR-effect frames are PNG sequences of at most 24 frames at a fixed 12 fps, frames <= 480x480, whole package <= 5 MB (<= 2 MB recommended).

label: WeChat (微信)
containerCodec: MP4 (documented for the WeChat official-account/Official Platform API video path, 10 MB). Container list for ordinary personal-chat sends is NOT published by Tencent.
maxSizeNote: NO primary-source figure for personal-chat sends. What IS primary: the WeChat Official Platform (公众号) media API limits video to 10 MB with MP4, images to 10 MB (2 MB for temporary media), and a separate chunked video-upload API documents 'filesize 最大2G' (2 GB) with 1 MB chunks. Third-party sources attribute '25 MB in-chat video / 5 min / ~200 MB via File' to Tencent customer service, but no Tencent-hosted page stating this could be read - treat as UNVERIFIED.
dimensions: Not published for personal chat. WeChat Channels (视频号) requires aspect ratio between 0.33 and 3.0 and recommends 16:9 or 9:16.
note: HONEST GAP - and an important structural one. Tencent does not publish personal-chat attachment limits in any readable primary source, and WeChat is several distinct products with different numbers: personal chat, WeCom (企业微信), Official Accounts (公众号), and Channels (视频号). Verified primary figures from the paths that DO publish: official-account permanent material accepts image 10 MB (bmp/png/jpeg/jpg/gif), video 10 MB (MP4 only), thumbnail 64 KB (JPG); temporary media image 2 MB / video 10 MB; and the chunked video upload API accepts up to 2 GB. WeChat Channels (视频号) separately documents: video up to 2 GB, 3 s to 60 min from mobile (30 min on older phones) or 3 s to 8 h from desktop, 1080p+ recommended, ratio 0.33-3.0, and that H.265 video cannot be published from desktop (findeross.weixin.qq.com help page). WeCom documents: PC files up to 10 GB (compressed archives 3 GB), mobile single file up to 4 GB, and images over 20 MB (JPG) or 5 MB (GIF) are sent as generic files. Do NOT put a personal-WeChat video preset in the data file until a Tencent source is found.
maxSizeText: not published for personal chat; Official Platform API: video 10 MB / image 10 MB; chunked video upload up to 2 GB

label: QQ (腾讯QQ)
containerCodec: Official QQ Bot API v2: inline video must be MP4; images accept png/jpg (the message docs also list gif/webp/bmp); files accept any type.
maxSizeNote: On the official Bot API: image soft limit 20 MB / hard limit 200 MB; video soft limit 30 MB / hard limit 200 MB; file hard limit 200 MB. Exceeding the SOFT limit silently downgrades the attachment to a plain FILE; exceeding the HARD limit returns error 850031. For ordinary consumer QQ chat, Tencent publishes NO limit at all - third-party claims of 200 MB-4 GB are unreliable and are not used here.
dimensions: Not published.
note: The verified numbers are from QQ's official BOT developer documentation, which is a developer surface, not what a normal user sees when they attach a video in QQ chat. That distinction matters for an export preset: if the destination is 'QQ chat' as a user knows it, Tencent publishes no spec and no primary source exists. Consumer QQ does compress in-chat photos and videos and offers an '原图' (original) option to bypass it. The soft-limit-downgrades-to-file behaviour is the notable mechanic: exceed 30 MB with a video and it stops being a playable video and becomes a file attachment, which is a silent user-visible downgrade rather than an error.
maxSizeText: Bot API soft 20 MB image / 30 MB video (silently becomes a file), hard 200 MB; consumer chat: not published

label: QQ sticker (表情)
containerCodec: Main sticker: GIF. Thumbnail: PNG. Icons: PNG.
maxSizeNote: Main GIF <= 300 KB each. Thumbnail PNG: the archived official table says <= 200 KB while its own body text says <= 20 KB - the official page CONTRADICTS ITSELF, so this one value is not trustworthy. Icons <= 10 KB.
dimensions: Main sticker EXACTLY 300x300. Thumbnail EXACTLY 300x300. Icons 18x18 (x2), 60x60, 200x200, plus irregular 126x112 / 94x112 / 71x56. Fixed set of 16 stickers.
note: PROVENANCE WARNING: this spec is an ARCHIVED snapshot of Tencent's official 腾讯原创开放平台 design page dating from 2023 or earlier; the live yuanchuang.qq.com page no longer loads. Treat it as a stale primary source. Verified from it: 300x300 exact, main GIF <= 300 KB, transparent background required ('无色透明底') with a 3 px white stroke, first frame must be a complete still used as the preview, fixed set of 16. NOT verified: the thumbnail KB cap (page self-contradicts), whether QQ re-encodes on publish, and animated container beyond GIF. The 3 px white stroke requirement is unusual and worth honouring if we ever target QQ stickers.

label: KakaoTalk emoticon
containerCodec: Animated emoticons must be animated WebP built with Kakao's own WebP Animator tool - not GIF, and non-Animator WebP may fail to run. Still emoticons are PNG. Brand emoticon: emot = WebP, keyboard thumbnail = PNG, web detail title = GIF.
maxSizeNote: 650 KB per item for brand emoticons (both the emot and the app-detail title). Kakao's public animator page does NOT publish a per-file KB cap for ordinary emoticon submissions - it caps FRAME COUNT instead. Extra creator-proposal KB caps circulating in Korean blogs (150 KB, etc.) are third-party and unverified.
dimensions: Moving emoticon 360x360; mini 180x180; big 540x540 / 300x540 / 540x300. Frame counts: max 24 frames (big and moving), max 18 frames (mini). Brand emoticons: 360x360, per-frame duration 0.05-2.0 s.
note: Kakao caps FRAMES rather than seconds for ordinary emoticons, which is unusual and matters for our preset model - there is no documented maxDurationSec, so substitute a frame cap. Brand emoticon numbers (650 KB, loops = 4, 0.05-2.0 s per frame, RGB at 72 dpi, transparent background for the emot, #ffffff for the web detail title) come from Kakao's official brand-emoticon guide (kakaobusiness.gitbook.io/main/ad/other-ad/brandemoticon/undefined). Loop behaviour differs by surface: WebP emoticons and titles loop 4 times, while a GIF web-detail title loops infinitely. Also note that in chat the last frame is where playback STOPS by default, so this is not an endless loop like a Telegram sticker. The requirement to use Kakao's own WebP Animator is the single most important fact: an arbitrary animated WebP we generate may not be accepted.
maxDurationText: no time cap — frame cap instead (<=24 frames big/moving, <=18 mini)

label: KakaoTalk
containerCodec: PC file send accepts images jpg/jpeg/gif/bmp/png/tif/tga/psd and video mp4/m4v/avi/asf/wmv/mkv/ts/mpg/mpeg/mov/flv/ogv.
maxSizeNote: 300 MB per file for PC file send. Separately, photos sent AS photos are limited to 9 MB each with a maximum of 10 at a time. Mobile limits are NOT published by Kakao.
dimensions: Not published.
note: The 300 MB figure and the container list are from Kakao's own help pages (PC file send). Kakao states that a video sent via File is 'sent in its original form and does not have to be converted', so the File path does not transcode - unlike photos sent as photos, which are compressed, and unlike mobile sends which auto-compress. The 9 MB/10-at-a-time photo limits come from Kakao's help (cs.kakao.com/helps_html/1073181265). UNVERIFIED: mobile attachment limits, whether alpha survives, and accepted codecs beyond the container list.

label: Reddit
containerCodec: MP4 and MOV (stated by Reddit). Reddit also has a native GIF converter that turns an uploaded video into an MP4 gif, so a GIF is not the ideal thing to upload - upload MP4 and let Reddit produce the looping MP4.
maxSizeNote: NOT VERIFIED. Reddit publishes no file-size limit on any page I could read: support.reddithelp.com refused to be crawled (timeout / 404 on the article routes) and the 2017 launch announcement states only a duration limit. Third-party sources claim 1 GB for native video, a 100 MB cap for animated GIFs on i.redd.it, and 20 MB for static images, but NONE of these is confirmed by a Reddit primary source, so do not encode them as facts.
dimensions: posts: not published. Comments: min 50x50 px, min bitrate 1 KB/s.
note: HONEST GAP, partly filled. Reddit's help centre publishes video specs ONLY for video in COMMENTS, and that article is the sole current Reddit-owned video spec I could reach (support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/48109333836692, body re-fetched 2026-09-11): under 1 GB (ideally under 300 MB), 2-180 s, minimum 50x50 px, minimum bitrate 1 KB/s. For native video POSTS Reddit publishes NO current spec: the only Reddit-owned post-video numbers are in a 2017 product announcement (redditinc.com/news/video-is-coming-to-reddit) which states 'Allowed video file types are MP4 and MOV, with a maximum length of 15 minutes' — nine years old, so treat MP4/MOV and 15 min as probable but stale. The widely cited '1 GB / 15 min' for POSTS is not on any official Reddit page I could fetch; Reddit Ads help separately documents 1 GB / 2-15 min / MP4-MOV / max 30 FPS for AD creatives, which is the advertising surface and must not be presented as the organic limit. Custom emoji (community flair) IS documented: 64 KB per emoji, max 128x128 px (64x64 recommended), up to 100 at once and 5,000 per community, though the accepted file formats are not listed (support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/15484571863188, edited 2025-10-24). No user-facing sticker format spec exists. Subreddit AutoModerator rules routinely impose far tighter caps than the platform. Reddit does not accept GIF as a first-class native video format; prefer MP4/MOV.
maxSizeText: organic posts: not published. Comments (the only published video spec): under 1 GB, ideally under 300 MB
maxDurationText: posts: 15 min per a 2017 announcement only; comments: 2-180 s
